projects.name: REA
projects.oneliner: One MCP server for reverse engineering apps, binaries, and runtime behavior from any coding agent.
projects.why: 370K total stars and still the most-starred AI repo on GitHub weekly trending; reverse engineering remains one of the hottest agent use cases.

projects.name: Superpowers
projects.oneliner: Agentic skills framework and methodology for building agent workflows.
projects.why: 309K total stars; the largest skills framework in the Claude ecosystem, with a growing library of community-contributed skills.

projects.name: OpenCode
projects.oneliner: The open-source coding agent with terminal TUI, desktop app, and IDE extension, model-agnostic.
projects.why: 220K total stars and over 1,000 contributors; the leading open-source alternative to proprietary coding agents.

projects.name: TradingAgents
projects.oneliner: Multi-agent LLM trading framework that simulates a trading firm with analyst, researcher, and risk manager agents.
projects.why: 119K total stars; the largest open-source AI trading framework as agent-driven finance draws more builders.

projects.name: Gemini CLI
projects.oneliner: Google's official terminal AI agent powered by the Gemini API.
projects.why: 109K total stars with 701 contributors; Google's answer to Claude Code, now a fixture of the AI developer toolkit.

projects.name: VoiceStudio
projects.oneliner: Open-source voice cloning, transcription, and text-to-speech, positioned as an ElevenLabs alternative.
projects.why: 72K total stars and still climbing; voice AI demand keeps growing as developers look for self-hosted alternatives.

projects.name: Hyperframes
projects.oneliner: Renders video from HTML, built for agents that need to produce and edit video programmatically.
projects.why: 66K total stars; from HeyGen, bridging AI agents and video production with a growing contributor base.

projects.name: DeepTutor
projects.oneliner: Lifelong personalized tutoring agent that adapts to each student over time.
projects.why: 51K total stars; from HKU Data Science Lab, one of the first research-backed AI tutoring agents to gain wide adoption.

projects.name: Knowledge Work Plugins
projects.oneliner: Anthropic's official plugins for Claude Cowork, covering productivity and collaboration workflows.
projects.why: 34K stars; Anthropic's growing plugin ecosystem is drawing both enterprise and community contributors.

projects.name: SkillSpector
projects.oneliner: Security scanner that analyzes AI agent skills for vulnerabilities before they run.
projects.why: 23K stars; NVIDIA entering the agent-skills security space shows the ecosystem is maturing beyond code to safety tooling.

projects.name: OpenMausBot
projects.oneliner: Open-source Grok bot alternative with customizable model and sandbox support.
projects.why: 8K total stars; a growing self-hosted option for teams that want a Grok-powered bot without vendor lock-in.

projects.name: ThinkRail
projects.oneliner: JetBrains' IDE for vibe coding with its Pi AI coding agent.
projects.why: 6.4K stars; JetBrains entering the vibe-coding space with a dedicated IDE signals that agent-native development is going mainstream.

projects.name: Skill Recorder
projects.oneliner: Records work sessions and converts them into reusable AI agent skills.
projects.why: 5.6K stars; Microsoft's approach to skill creation through demonstration rather than code.

projects.name: Rakazo
projects.oneliner: Open-source alternative to Grok Bot where you choose the model and sandbox.
projects.why: 5.3K stars; the leading self-hosted alternative to SpaceXAI's Grok Bot.

projects.name: jev-browser-wingman
projects.oneliner: Hands an agent's browser clicks to TypeSafe's Jev, which picks the element for each step.
projects.why: One of the first third-party tools built on System One models; Jev's developer ecosystem is still small but growing.
